title: Pakistani Fashion Trends 2026: The Rise of Luxury Pret and Bridal Couture
author: Sillhouete Studio
excerpt: Explore the emerging aesthetic in women fashion: minimal embellishments with maximalist silhouette cuts, raw silk revivals, and bespoke international sizing.
content:

title: Rituals Inside a Muslim Wedding Ceremony: Bridal Styling & Traditions
author: Sillhouete Bridal Studio
excerpt: An insider look into traditional Pakistani wedding ceremonies — from Mehndi and Mayun to the sacred Nikkah, Barat, and Walima — and what each bridal palette signifies.
content:
Pakistani weddings are renowned for their vibrant festivities, deep emotional moments, and grand couture. Each celebration has its own distinct dress code and cultural charm.

The Joyous Colors of Mehndi & Mayun

Yellows, tangerines, lime greens, and jewel tones take center stage. Fabrics are lightweight yet ornate, accented with gotapatti, mirrors, and floral jewelry.

The Sacred Elegance of the Nikkah

Modern brides increasingly gravitate toward serene ivory, soft blush, and champagne hues adorned with delicate silver zardozi and pearl embellishments.

The Grandeur of the Barat

Traditional royal crimson, maroon, and scarlet lehengas hand-embossed with dabka, kora, and precious stones embody timeless bridal grandeur.

The Sophistication of the Walima

Pastel mints, dusty lilacs, and ice blues with flowing trains and contemporary cuts provide a stunning finale to wedding celebrations.

title: Kurta vs Kurti: Which Silhouette Suits You Best?
author: Sillhouete Editorial
excerpt: Understanding the distinction between traditional kurtas and modern kurtis, tailoring techniques, and how to style them for daily elegance and festive celebrations.
content:
When it comes to South Asian fashion, two terms often used interchangeably are kurta and kurti. While they share heritage roots, the cut, drape, and styling of each create distinct fashion statements.

The Traditional Elegance of the Kurta

A classic kurta typically features knee-length or calf-length hems, straight or slightly A-line cuts, and long side slits. Traditionally paired with straight trousers, shalwars, or culottes, it provides an elongated and graceful frame. At Sillhouete, our luxury pret kurtas feature fine resham embroidery, tonal zari, and pure raw silk fabrics.

The Versatility of the Modern Kurti

Kurtis are shorter in length, falling anywhere from the hip to mid-thigh. They are contemporary, playful, and easily paired with denim, cigarette pants, or tulip shalwars. Ideal for semi-formal brunches or effortless workplace sophistication.

Fabrics and Styling

For warm summer days, lightweight organza and lawn with delicate hand embroidery are perfect. For evening gatherings, raw silk with organza dupatta trims gives a regal touch.
